text:
alex: Heads-up: after landing the exports refactor, a few downstream TS projects reported type resolution failures when importing subpaths. Example from a customer sample: `import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk/chat'` fails to find types.
tanya: hmm. do we still have a `types` field in package.json? some tools prefer explicit subpath typing exports.
alex: package.json currently has `\"types\": \"dist/esm/index.d.ts\"` and exports like:
```json
\"exports\": {
  \"./chat\": {
    \"import\": \"./dist/esm/chat/index.js\",
    \"require\": \"./dist/cjs/chat/index.js\"
  },
  \"./package.json\": \"./package.json\"
}
```

alex: there are no typings under `./chat` export, so TS + bundlers that check package exports don't find .d.ts.
kevin: yeah TS 5+ and some bundlers consult exports subpaths for types. If no `types` subpath exists they can fail with `Could not find a declaration file for module`.
li: quick repro: consumer app using pnpm + workspace protocol. TS error shows `Cannot find module '@redwood-inference/sdk/chat' or its corresponding type declarations.`
tanya: two fixes: add `types` entries in exports subpath, or add `typesVersions`/index.d.ts map. I prefer explicit typing subpaths so our package consumers get proper resolution.
kevin: propose adding under exports: `\"./chat\": { \"types\": \"./dist/types/chat/index.d.ts\", ... }`. Also add a top-level `types` fallback.
alex: also saw weirdness with ESM/CJS: some bundlers resolve `./chat` to CJS entry and then TS tries to pick types next to CJS and misses ESM .d.ts. So we need to make typings discovery independent of JS entry.
li: Deno and Bun users complained too. Bun's resolver looks at `exports` conditions differently and won't apply types fallback.
tanya: actionables:
- add `types` property on every exports subpath that currently exposes public subpaths (kevin)
- generate `dist/types/*` during build and include in npm package (kevin)
- add `typesVersions` mapping for older TS toolchains (tanya)
- add a tiny CI check that installs the package and runs `tsc --noEmit` against a handful of sample imports (li)

kevin: for compatibility we can also add an explicit `./package.json` export pointing to package.json (we already have it) and include `types` in package.json top-level. But explicit subpath typings are the most robust.
li: sample snippet we can include in the SDK package.json patch:
```json
\"exports\": {
  ".": {
    \"import\": \"./dist/esm/index.js\",
    \"require\": \"./dist/cjs/index.js\",
    \"types\": \"./dist/types/index.d.ts\"
  },
  \"./chat\": {
    \"import\": \"./dist/esm/chat/index.js\",
    \"require\": \"./dist/cjs/chat/index.js\",
    \"types\": \"./dist/types/chat/index.d.ts\"
  }
}
```

tanya: also add docs note: \"If you use bundlers targeting Edge or browser, prefer the ESM path and ensure your package.json contains `module`/`browser` fields or `edge`/`browser` conditions in exports.\" small FAQ entry.
alex: i'll open a PR with patch and include a small consumer tsc sample in examples/types-check. will tag #DEVEX-421.
kevin: let's also night- run a script that resolves exports using `resolve.exports` across node, bun, deno to detect mismatches.
li: thanks. FYI I posted the minimal repro in the ticket. devex-bot: Reminder: link PRs to ticket #DEVEX-421 and add `examples/types-check` to CI.
tanya: sweet. i'll help wire up the CI job. alex: will ping when PR is up :rocket:
